note: ONE vector file for every verifier. Each verifier's test builds a real signed record of the kind named (a decision, a statement, a cease: a record-only act, or a grant: a record shaped as a caller grant, which signs no verdict), whose signed metadata carries none of verdict, exec_not_after, exp, not_after, nbf, decided_at except the members given under metadata, exactly as given (a null is a present null). A deadline is reported for two kinds of record, by what the signed metadata carries (members): a decision that allowed (the verdict is the text allow; its deadline is the first present member of its end list, its start the first of its start list) and a statement (a record of the statement kind, requisition.lab.statement.v0, with no verdict member, and exp). A record of another kind that signs exp and no verdict is no statement. Every other record has no window. The record passes; the last lines of the pass are pass_line and then lines, for the time given as --at (null: no time given). Each value under malformed_at is refused as a usage error before anything is checked. On a failure pass_line is not printed. No exit depends on a time. Each row under unknown_arguments is a list of arguments added to a valid invocation: it is refused as a usage error before anything is checked, because a verifier that skipped an argument it does not know would pass in silence where the caller asked for a comparison. Each name under unknown_options is the same row for a verifier that is a library: an option it does not take, given with a time as its value, is refused.
pass_line: A pass shows these bytes were signed under the key you supplied. It is not permission to act. Whether an action may run is decided by the issuing system when it runs.
